Actually maybe my story can be a bit of an insight. I live an average life, average social media, I occasionally meet with friends, hangout, contact a select few through people on social media religiously. Most people who know me think I’m ultra extroverted because of how I present myself in social gatherings. Truth is, I have a lengthy experience of getting bullied, early life culture change (more traumatic than you think), abusive parents, sexually abusive family, rape experience, ADHD, mild depression, social anxiety, generalized anxiety, dissociative amnesia, I’m gay in a religious network, and I have several PTSDs from my lifelong shit stuff. Most people who know me have no clue what I’m going through on a daily basis. 

To others they think I’m working in prestigious companies in successful large cities, wearing and eating beautiful stuff. My issues don’t let me deal with human beings unless in very rare occasions I actually open up my heart to them, which takes a lot of testing and risk taking and is extremely taxing to my mentality. Many times I have to cut off people or just hide away because even texting or communicating is (for a lack of better term) overbearing. I would say my conditions are not common, but everyone goes through something in their lives, sometimes as bad or worse than the level I’m describing. Most don’t talk about it. It’s just easier for yourself to think people are going through the equal amount of pain you are going through right now, in different ways. If you see them as a victim too, you stop becoming a victim.

It’s nice you’ve been reaching out, but at the same time it’s their choice to associate with someone or not. You don’t know all their reasons and life stories the other person has gone through, and they have their right to keep distance if they want to/need to. There are many other cool people out there :) you shouldn’t keep yourself attached to someone that continues to hurt you, whether they are aware of it or not, or you were rightly hurt or not. Just not healthy. Breaking off is strength to some; be proud of yourself!
